segments.text: Okay, essay. The fiber essay. I have about two thousand words and I have, like, nine pages of notes, so the job today is structure, not research. No more research.
What is the argument. Um. The argument is that towns under, say, twenty thousand people should build and own their own fiber.

No, that is the conclusion. The argument is why. The argument is that the incumbents will never build there, because the math does not work for them, and the math does work for a town because a town does not need a return, it needs a utility.
That is pretty good actually. The math does not work for them and does work for you. That is the thesis in one sentence.
So, sections. I had five. Let me go through them and see which ones earn a place.
One, the history of rural electrification, the co-ops in the thirties. Which is the obvious parallel and everyone uses it, but it is obvious because it is right.
Two, the cost numbers. Per home passed, per home connected, what the town bonds look like, the twenty year payback.
Three, the examples that worked. Chattanooga, obviously, but Chattanooga is a city, so, the smaller ones. The ones in Vermont, the one in North Dakota.
Four, the examples that did not work. Which is the honest section. Provo, mostly. Provo built it and sold it to a tech company for a dollar.
Five, the policy stuff, the state laws that ban towns from doing this, which, there are like eighteen states.
Okay that is five. Two thousand words divided by five is four hundred each, which is nothing, so, something has to go.
I think history goes. Or, not goes, it becomes two sentences in the intro. Everyone knows the electrification story. I do not need four hundred words on it.
So four sections. Cost, worked, did not work, policy.
Hm, the order though. If I open with cost that is dry. If I open with the examples that worked that is a story, which is better.
But then cost second, and then did not work third, and the did not work section is the one where the whole essay could fall apart.
Because the strongest objection is just, Provo. Provo tried this exact thing and it failed and they sold it for a dollar. If I cannot answer that, there is no essay. Anyway, policy section.

Policy is, um, the eighteen states. The point there is that the ban exists because the incumbents lobbied for it, and that is itself evidence for the thesis. If the math did not work for towns, you would not need a law.
Oh, that is actually the best point in the whole thing. If it could not work they would not have banned it.
So maybe policy is not last. Maybe policy is, like, the turn. The place where the essay stops describing and starts arguing.
Okay so, let me re do the order. Worked, cost, policy, did not work? No. You cannot end on failure.
Worked, did not work, cost, policy. So the failure comes early, I deal with it, and then the cost section is the answer to it, because the answer to Provo is that Provo over built and over borrowed.
And then policy is the closer, the if it could not work they would not ban it line, and then a short conclusion.
Yeah. Yeah that is the shape. The failure is the question and the cost section is the answer and the policy section is the proof.

Now, Provo. What actually went wrong there. From my notes. They built in two thousand four, they bonded for, um, thirty nine million, and they tried to run it like a business, with a wholesale model where other companies sold the service.
And the wholesale thing is what killed it. Not the fiber. The fiber is still there, it is still being used. The model was wrong.
So my answer to Provo is, Provo proves the fiber works, it is the business model that failed, and the model I am proposing is the utility model, not the wholesale model.
Is that too convenient? Like, am I just defining away the failure?
A little. But the Vermont ones used the utility model and they are fine, so, it is not just a definition, there is a comparison.

Okay. Word counts. Worked, four hundred. Did not work, four hundred. Cost, six hundred, because that is where the numbers are and numbers take space. Policy, four hundred. Intro and conclusion, two hundred total.
That is two thousand. Good.
The opening line. I want to open on a specific town. The one in North Dakota, the one with eleven hundred people, where the co-op did it.
Something like, in a town of eleven hundred people in North Dakota, you can get a gigabit for sixty dollars a month. Then the next line is, in most towns that size you cannot get anything at all.
That is okay. It is a little, um, it is a little magazine-y. But it is a draft.
Right. Structure done. Worked, did not work, cost, policy. Two sentences of history in the intro. Provo as the question, utility model as the answer. Open on North Dakota.
I will write the did not work section first because it is the scary one.
Okay, going.
